questions.q: What did Nadella keep secret while working at Microsoft?
a: His part-time MBA enrollment in Chicago
His application to a rival technology company
His plan to leave for a career in cricket
His work on a competing operating system
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he did not want to endanger his job, so he kept his weekend MBA studies private.

questions.q: What does Nadella do when he feels intimidated?
a: He treats it as a signal that it is time to compete
He steps back and lets more experienced people lead
He asks his coach for a different position
He avoids the situation until he feels confident
questions.why: Lesson 2 says his first rule is that feeling intimidated means it is time to compete.

questions.q: What did the captain do that helped Nadella regain his confidence?
a: He kept bowling until he took a wicket, then gave Nadella the ball
He replaced Nadella with a stronger bowler for the final overs
He told Nadella to study the Australians' batting technique
He moved Nadella to a different position in the field
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the captain persisted until he got a wicket, then handed the ball back to lift Nadella.

questions.q: What did Nadella show the audience at the Salesforce event?
a: An iPhone running Microsoft software
A new Microsoft phone with no apps
A prototype of a Windows laptop
A video of Microsoft's latest game console
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes him displaying an iPhone with Microsoft programs such as Outlook and Skype running on it.

questions.q: How does Nadella approach rival companies like Apple?
a: He looks for ways to work with them
He tries to defeat them at any cost
He ignores them and focuses inward
He copies their products as closely as possible
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he believes cooperating with competitors benefits both Microsoft and the wider world.
